issues.legal_issue: Remuneration received under a bank treasurership arrangement is salary rather than business profit when the arrangement, considered as a whole, establishes employment under the bank’s control and supervision.
material_facts: The treasurer received a fixed monthly salary for work at multiple bank branches.
The bank directed how the treasurer’s duties were to be performed and exercised control over the treasurer and the cash department staff.
The treasurer’s work formed part of the bank’s operations; the bank could require staff changes and terminate the treasurer’s services.
The treasurer was responsible for losses caused by negligence or default in the performance of the duties, including defaults by cash department staff.
issues.conclusion: The treasurer was a servant of the bank, and the emoluments were salary assessable under section 7 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, rather than profits and gains of business assessable under section 10.
issues.legal_principle: The agreement must be assessed as a whole, having regard to the nature of the work and the employer’s control and supervision. Relevant indicia include the power of selection, payment of remuneration, control over the method of work, and the power of suspension or dismissal; no single test applies in every case. The Court relied on Shivanandan Sharma v. Punjab National Bank Ltd. and Dharangadhara Chemical Works Ltd. v. State of Saurashtra, and referred to Cassidy v. Ministry of Health and Short v. J. and Henderson Ltd.

rule.if: employment_income_classification_case and (employer_controls_work and work_integral_to_employer_business and regular_remuneration)

predicates.employment_income_classification_case: The proceeding concerns whether remuneration received for work is employment income or business profit for income-tax purposes.
predicates.employer_controls_work: The employer directs or supervises how the worker performs the duties, having regard to the nature of the work.
predicates.work_integral_to_employer_business: The worker performs duties as an integrated part of the employer’s business rather than as an outside service provider.
predicates.regular_remuneration: The worker receives regular remuneration for performing the duties.

issues.definition: When an income-classification proceeding concerns work controlled by an employer, integrated into that employer’s business, and compensated regularly, the remuneration is treated as salary rather than business profit.

issues.legal_issue: Remuneration earned by a member of a Hindu undivided family belongs to that member rather than the family when the earning depends on personal fitness and family property was merely furnished as security, without family-funded training, expenditure, or other detriment enabling the appointment.
material_facts: The treasurer was a member and karta of a Hindu undivided family and had worked for the bank as an overseer before becoming treasurer.
His prior experience and his application for the post indicated personal fitness for the treasurership.
There was no evidence that family funds had paid for particular training or that family expenditure or other detriment enabled his appointment.
The treasurer furnished joint-family property as security for his responsibilities to the bank.
issues.conclusion: The mere furnishing of joint-family property as security did not make the treasurer’s salary income of the Hindu undivided family; it was his individual income.
issues.legal_principle: A member’s earnings are not joint-family income merely because family property is exposed to risk by being given as security. The relevant question is whether family funds or property were used or subjected to detriment in a way that enabled the member to acquire the qualification, appointment, or earning capacity. The Court explained Gokul Chand v. Firm Hukum Chand Nath Mal as concerning family expenditure that equipped a member for a profession, and distinguished Commissioner of Income-tax v. Kalu Babu Lal Chand on its different facts, where the family funds, business, and appointment were linked.

rule.if: joint_family_income_attribution_case and personal_fitness_for_appointment and family_property_given_only_as_security and not family_funds_enabled_qualification

predicates.joint_family_income_attribution_case: The proceeding concerns whether a member’s earnings are income of a joint family or of the member individually.
predicates.personal_fitness_for_appointment: The member’s own experience, ability, or qualifications support the appointment or earning activity.
predicates.family_property_given_only_as_security: The family property was furnished as security for the member’s responsibilities, without another shown use that enabled the earning activity.
predicates.family_funds_enabled_qualification: Family funds or property were used or subjected to detriment to train, qualify, or otherwise enable the member to obtain the appointment or earning capacity.

issues.definition: When an attribution proceeding concerns earnings obtained through the member’s personal fitness, and family property served only as security without family-funded enablement, the earnings belong to the member rather than the family.
